daily_summary: 当日 4 个 commit 覆盖三条主线：(1) warp-specialize 的 noinline helper 上下文保持——通过新增 ttg.warp-id-offset 属性把每个 outlined helper 的有效 warp 数贯穿 LLVM 转换，并让 thread/warp ID 相对于调用分区计算，修复 warp 特化 Gluon 代码的索引错误和 TMA 拷贝不完整；(2) E8M0 缩放解码修复——字节 0 表示 2^-127、字节 255 表示 NaN，在编译器 lowering、解释器、独立 upcast、Hopper FP4 packed 布局和 scaled reduction 中统一按 max + FMA 语义修正，并新增 Blackwell 原生 cvt.rn.bf16x2.ue8m0x2 路径；(3) triton_kernels 支持未缩放 FP8 E4M3 与 FP16/BF16 混精 matmul，放宽 Hopper 权重布局和 dtype 检查、调整 tile/显存规划；(4) 测试修复：把 AMD Gluon 的 noinline 共享分配测试从 NVIDIA 专属门控改造成可通过 THREAD_PER_WARP 参数在 HIP 上运行，以及把 AMD CDNA5 测试中误写的比较表达式改为 assert。整体以 bugfix 与精度/正确性修复为主，另有少量 test 与性能相关改动。
ascend_impact_summary: 当日 4 个 commit 对 triton-ascend 的影响集中在 commit 1 与 commit 2。commit 1 修改了 lib/Conversion/TritonGPUToLLVM/Utility.cpp、include/triton/Dialect/TritonGPU/IR/Dialect.h、lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/IR/Dialect.cpp 与 third_party/nvidia/NVGPUToLLVM，均属于 TTGIR→LLVM 的 NVIDIA/AMD 专属 lowering 路径和 TTGIR 方言属性扩展，triton-ascend 走 TritonToLinalg 而非 TritonGPUToLLVM，且不继承 TargetInfoBase，因此不破坏其编译链；新增的是可选属性，不改变既有 op/type 定义，属于间接、无破坏性变更。commit 2 修改了 include/triton/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/DecomposeScaledBlocked.h、lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/DecomposeScaledBlocked.cpp、third_party/amd/*、python/triton/runtime/interpreter.py 与 python/triton/tools/mxfp.py：其中 DecomposeScaledBlocked 的 scaleTo16/extendAndBroadcastScale 增加了 handleNan 参数，属于 C++ 内部 protected 方法签名扩展，Ascend 不调用该 pass；interpreter.py 的 _prepare_dot_scaled_operand/_dot_scaled_scale_to_f32 是 AscendInterpreterBuilder 复用的公共符号，其语义变化（E8M0 字节 0/255 解码语义修正、compute_type 传递）会同步影响 Ascend 的 CPU 解释执行结果，但属功能一致的修正而非破坏；python/triton/tools/mxfp.py 新增 fp8e8m0_to_float32 为纯增量，无破坏。commit 3 与 commit 4 仅涉及 python/triton_kernels 和 AMD/NVIDIA 测试，对 triton-ascend 无影响。总体无需改动 triton-ascend 代码，但由于解释器 dot_scaled 语义变化，建议补充相应的解释器回归用例。

commits.comment: 本 commit 修复 warp-specialized Gluon 代码中 noinline helper 丢失 warp 上下文的问题。实现上新增 ttg.warp-id-offset 属性（include/triton/Dialect/TritonGPU/IR/Dialect.h），在 AllocateWarpGroups pass 中通过新增的 annotateWarpIdOffsets 遍历调用图，为每个 non-kernel 函数按 caller 的 warp group 起始 warp id 取模该 helper 的 warp 数算出 offset，冲突时报错；FuncOpToLLVM（通用与 AMD 版本）改用 lookupNumWarps 统一写回 ws_num_warps；Dialect.cpp 的 maybeLookupNumWarps 在 FunctionOpInterface 上读取 ws_num_warps，使 outlined helper 保留自身 warp 数；Utility.cpp 的 getThreadId 与 NVGPU/AMD 的 WarpIdOpToLLVM 在函数级 offset 存在时，对 thread/warp id 做 sub + and 掩码得到分区相对 ID；NVGPUToLLVMPass.cpp 同样处理 warpId 偏移。测试补充 Gluon test_warp_specialize_noinline_ids 以及 tritongpu_to_llvm / AMD gfx1250 / amd 的 FileCheck 用例，验证 1-warp helper 的 TMA 拷贝与 8-warp helper 的相对索引。风险点：annotateWarpIdOffsets 用 getWarpGroupStartWarpId 回退到 caller 的既有 offset，若调用图中存在同一 callee 被不同模余数的分区调用则直接报错（合理但可能对已有代码产生新的编译失败）；getThreadId 依赖 getWarpGroupStartThreadId 与函数属性二者取其一，需保证嵌套 noinline 链条上 offset 传播正确。整体是中等风险的 TTGIR→LLVM 修复，但仅覆盖 NV/AMD 路径。

ascend_impact.functionality: 无影响。变更集中在 TTGIR 方言属性扩展（新增可选 ttg.warp-id-offset）、AllocateWarpGroups（TritonGPU warp specialization pass）、TritonGPUToLLVM 的 Utility/FuncOpToLLVM 以及 NVGPUToLLVM、AMD 的 WarpIdOpToLLVM。triton-ascend 的 lowering 走 TritonToLinalg 路径，不使用 TritonGPUToLLVM 和 TargetInfoBase，也不使用 AllocateWarpGroups；TritonGPU IR 中新增的属性为可选且不影响既有 op/type/verifier 语义，Ascend 的 TTIR→Linalg 转换链不感知该属性。
ascend_impact.testing: 无影响。所涉 lit 测试（test/Conversion/tritongpu_to_llvm.mlir、test/Conversion/amd/*、test/Conversion/tritongpu_to_llvm_gfx1250.mlir）与 Gluon 测试均为 NVIDIA/AMD 专属，Ascend 不运行。

commits.message:
[GPU] Preserve warp context in noinline helpers (#11673)

Preserve each outlined helper's effective warp count through LLVM
conversion and make thread and warp IDs relative to the calling
partition. This fixes incorrect indices and incomplete TMA copies from
warp-specialized Gluon code.

[DOCS] Fix broken link to plugins README in top-level README (#11700)

The plugins directory was moved from lib/Plugins/ to examples/plugins/
in commit 70723756e932 (#8523), but the link in the top-level README was
not updated, resulting in a 404 error.

Update the link from lib/Plugins/README.md to
examples/plugins/README.md.

commits.message:
[Triton] Fix E8M0 scale decoding (#11624)

Fix by @Maratyszcza

E8M0 byte `0` represents `2^-127`, and byte `255` represents NaN.
Several software decoders treated these as zero or infinity. Correct
both encodings across compiler lowering, the interpreter, standalone
upcasts, packed Hopper FP4 layouts, and scaled reductions. For example,
a 128-term dot product of BF16 `2^112` and FP8 `256` with scale byte `0`
must return `1`; the old decoder returns `0`.

The fix covers integer E8M0 scales with FP4 E2M1 and FP8 E4M3/E5M2
values. Scaled reductions also cover BF16 and FP32 inputs. BF16 and FP32
decoding preserve the minimum value; FP16 still rounds it to zero. H100
software decomposition is affected, including two-scaled FP8 matmuls.
Native NVIDIA block-scaled MMA keeps its existing path, and a zero
floating-point scale remains zero.

Numeric software decoders zero-extend and shift the scale byte, preserve
the BF16/FP32 minimum with an integer maximum, and use `fma(scale, +0,
scale)` to turn the infinity encoding into NaN. The generic FP16 path
omits the minimum correction because that value rounds to zero. The FMA
precedes FP16 narrowing; generic dot decomposition also decodes before
scale broadcasting. Packed Hopper decoding applies the same operations
to two BF16 lanes per instruction. The interpreter and AMD software
upcasts also normalize NaN scales. Signed-byte storage is reinterpreted
as unsigned before widening: byte `0x80` encodes `+2`, not `-2`.

The remaining exceptions preserve their existing contracts:

- Software `dot_scaled` omits explicit scale-NaN handling under
`fast_math=True`; Triton-to-Gluon's existing decomposition supports only
this mode.
- Native AMD conversion instructions consume encoded scales;
`dot_scaled` keeps its existing NaN mask after conversion. Direct
hardware upcasts retain the hardware decoding path, with added NaN-scale
regression tests.
- Saturating library upcasts restore scale NaNs after clamping, which
would otherwise erase them. An earlier FMA would be redundant.
- FPSan uses integer payload arithmetic, including the native UE8M0
conversion. Torch references retain an independent bit-mask decoder.

### Native Blackwell scale decoding

The shared `upcast_ue8m0_scale` helper uses
[`cvt.rn.bf16x2.ue8m0x2`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/#data-movement-and-conversion-instructions-cvt)
for BF16 on Blackwell. It decodes two scale bytes per instruction,
preserving both the minimum value and NaN. Scalar scales, FP16/FP32
outputs, and earlier GPUs use the portable decoder. FPSan preserves the
same integer payloads for both implementations.

Compared with the correct software decoder in [Merge main and resolve
MXFP test
imports](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/3bfb37d69a8264a854582ddd583b4aeaebf0d8cb),
[[NVIDIA] Use native UE8M0 decoding in kernel
helpers](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/ab6ac038ade3d0fb93693d7d7615673d940005d3)
lowers large FP4 → BF16 upcast latency by **3.7%** on GB300. Large E5M2
→ BF16 is **1.1% slower**; standalone scale decoding is unchanged.
Compiler `dot_scaled` decomposition keeps the max/FMA decoder: inserting
this packed inline assembly there caused extra layout and multiplication
work.

| UE8M0 → BF16 | 4194304 | 2.943 | 2.943 | 0.00% | 0.00% | 14→18 |

The comparison uses the same GB300, inputs, buffers, and ptxas 13.4.59,
with 32 launches per CUDA graph, 100 ms warmup, and 12 alternating AB/BA
pairs per process, repeated in a fresh process. Times cover complete GPU
kernels; allocation, compilation, and Python dispatch are excluded.
Upcasts use `64×128` tiles and scale bytes `124`–`129`; direct decoding
kernels use all scale encodings. Shared memory, scratch, and warmed
Torch allocation are unchanged, with no spills. Standalone upcast
register counts are unchanged; direct scale decoding uses four more
registers. Recompilation at the linked final head reproduces the
measured machine code and resource use.

### Compiler performance

Compare the [[TEST] Respect FP8 hardware limits in E8M0 boundary
tests](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/a457e6f19a5ad9b235b1c4b0053be30a41e1e736)
with [[Triton] Decode E8M0 scales with max and
FMA](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/b83896e9647810a9de14fb690c2c6999abd4ccf4),
holding inputs and buffers fixed. These measurements isolate the decoder
implementation within this PR and cover complete compiled `dot_scaled`
kernels.

**At these measured revisions: up to 20.4% lower latency on H100 and
33.6% on GB300.** The measured `fast_math` controls stay within 0.2%.
Native GB300 FP8 × FP8 has identical machine code.

All scaled operands use group-32 E8M0 bytes `124`–`129`; BF16/FP16
operands are unscaled. Tiles are `128×128×128`, with four warps, three
stages, and FP32 accumulation/output. `fast_math=False` unless labeled.
The two-scaled FP8 case uses software decomposition on H100 and native
scaled MMA on GB300.

Timings use 32 launches per CUDA graph, 200 ms warmup, and 12
alternating AB/BA pairs with approximately 50 ms per arm, followed by a
fresh-process repeat. Times are medians; changes are medians of paired
ratios. No clock locking or cache flushing. Allocation, compilation,
module loading, and graph creation are excluded. Binaries at the linked
revisions were checked against the measured kernels; changed `fast_math`
kernels were remeasured. † marks identical machine code and resource
usage; timing differences in these controls do not establish a speedup.

Affected GB300 mixed-input cases with a scaled left operand and
`fast_math=False` save 28–31 KiB of shared memory per block. H100 shared
memory is unchanged. Neither GPU adds global scratch or increases warmed
Torch memory usage. Resource use is not uniformly lower: H100's large
BF16 × FP4 case adds eight local bytes per thread, and some cases add
registers. Local storage is allocated capacity, not measured spill
traffic; the tables show these changes explicitly.

### Packed Hopper FP4 layouts

The packed Hopper decoder applies the minimum clamp and NaN-restoring
FMA to both BF16 lanes, preserving its four-scale packing. A 128-term
BF16 `2^118` × FP4 `4` matmul with scale byte `0` returns `1`. Scale
byte `255` produces NaN for nonzero FP4 inputs, where the old helper
produced infinity.

Compare the minimum-only decoder in [[KERNELS] Preserve minimum E8M0
scales in Hopper
layouts](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/0a1a9a317f5ea90a6b3fa9a3b2794aecd1ea637c)
with [[Triton] Complete E8M0 scale
decoding](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/2f3e1c6a2927cf5687f5872361d65f8cbcb5f943).
These measurements isolate the additional NaN handling with the same
native compiler. **At most 1.08% additional latency across two runs;
register, local/shared-memory, scratch, and warmed Torch memory usage
are unchanged.** A fresh build of the merged branch, with only the
decoder changes reverted for the baseline, reproduces the machine code
and resource counts of all 16 measured kernels.

<details>
<summary>H100: packed Hopper FP4 matmul measurements</summary>

| Kernel | Warps | M×N×K | Before µs | After µs | Change | First run |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Regular | 4 | 128×128×128 | 4.645 | 4.644 | -0.02% | -0.06% |
| Persistent | 4 | 128×128×128 | 9.194 | 9.247 | +0.57% | +0.55% |
| Regular | 4 | 2048×2048×1024 | 24.125 | 24.048 | -0.37% | -0.43% |
| Persistent | 4 | 2048×2048×1024 | 121.234 | 122.164 | +0.75% | +0.72%
|
| Regular | 8 | 128×256×128 | 6.985 | 6.987 | +0.04% | +0.05% |
| Persistent | 8 | 128×256×128 | 13.769 | 13.764 | -0.04% | +0.07% |
| Regular | 8 | 2048×2048×1024 | 28.307 | 28.474 | +0.59% | +0.95% |
| Persistent | 8 | 2048×2048×1024 | 96.703 | 97.726 | +1.06% | +1.08% |

</details>

Inputs are BF16 × FP4 with group-32 E8M0 scales `124`–`129` and FP32
output. Tiles are `128×(32·warps)×128`. Regular kernels use one pipeline
stage; persistent kernels use three stages with four warps and two with
eight warps. A separate three-stage regular configuration produces
incorrect results in both versions and on unmodified upstream code
predating this PR; it is excluded from these timings. All timed outputs
match an independent Torch reference exactly. Timing uses 32 launches
per CUDA graph and 12 alternating AB/BA pairs, approximately 50 ms per
arm, repeated in a fresh process.

### Validation

- A fresh build of the current head passes 145 library tests, 16
original minimum/zero-scale compiler regressions, 4,134 adversarial
matrix cases, and three FPSan tests on GB300. Coverage includes every
UE8M0 byte, signed-byte storage, both operand orders, FP16 boundaries,
and NaN-times-zero. NaN scales are excluded under `fast_math`. Native
and portable FPSan decoding agree for all 256 bytes.
- All 26 final GPU-code comparisons match: 16 `dot_scaled` kernels and
two FP32 reductions retain the software baseline's machine code and
resources; eight standalone upcast/decoder kernels reproduce the native
measurements above. Separate offline H100 checks retain identical
machine code and resources for 22 matmul/upcast kernels. The current
library matmul callers use the tile upcast helper only before Blackwell,
so they do not select its new native path.
- Hopper coverage includes every FP4 value with every scale byte, both
axes, four/eight warps, signed zero, and subnormals. Public
regular/persistent matmuls return NaN for scale `255`; the previous
helper returned infinity. The unchanged interpreter and Triton-to-Gluon
paths previously passed all 15 interpreter tests and 12 boundary cases.
Reduction tests check forward results and gradients.
- Rebuilt native code passes seven focused compiler files: three AMD
lowering files, generic max/FMA decoding, and common/AMD/NVIDIA FPSan.
Added runtime tests cover NaN scales with zero/nonzero FP4/E4M3/E5M2
inputs on CDNA3 and CDNA4. AMD runtime correctness has not been tested
locally on this revision; AMD performance was not measured.

Below CUDA capability 8.9, tests skip unsupported E4M3 conversion. E5M2
still checks NaN forward decoding and finite gradients; its NaN-gradient
case excludes the existing legacy FP8 downcast limitation.

The separate [[KERNELS] Reduce FP4/FP8 upcast
overhead](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/11644) remains
stacked on this correctness fix.

commits.comment: 本 commit 在 triton_kernels 中支持未缩放（unscaled）FP8 E4M3 与 FP16/BF16 的混合精度 matmul。核心实现是新增 matmul_dot helper（_common.py），在 tl.dot 之前按需把 FP8 E4M3 一侧 widen 到对侧 16 位类型，保留输入存储与 FP16 精度并使用 16 位 tensor core；_matmul.py 与 _p_matmul.py 用该 helper 替换原本直接的 SWAP_XW 分支。opt_flags_nvidia 新增 is_unscaled_mixed_fp8 判定，并据此放宽 Hopper 上原本强制列主序的 FP8 权重布局检查（matmul.py 中同步放宽），persistent 决策把 is_mixed_fp8 纳入 tiles_per_sm 的或条件，混合 FP8 且 rhs 为 FP8_E4M3FN 时默认开启 swap_xw 并可能交换 block_m/block_n，block_k 在 Hopper 未缩放混精下限制为 64 以降低寄存器压力；num_stages 计算把 widened RHS tile 与 epilogue scratch 纳入 shared memory 预算，并在比较完候选 epilogue 后再 clamp num_stages。AMD opt_flags 在未缩放路径下改用 max(lhs_width, rhs_width) 计算 128B cacheline 对齐的 block_k。_p_matmul.py 同时修复 gathered-input：把 offs_x_k 的 ki 分量并入每次迭代、把对齐基址指针 X 放在扁平化循环外，避免条件序言导致的偏移错误。风险点：混合 FP8/16-bit 会引入额外 widen 拷贝，H100 上大形状相对 BF16 有 0.81–0.85× 性能回退，且 FP8×FP16 的精度依赖 widen 时机正确；swap_xw 默认启用改变了部分既有 kernel 的布局，可能影响 bitwise invariance 场景（代码中以 enforce_bitwise_invariance 保护）。整体是 triton_kernels 库层的 feature + performance 折中，不涉及编译器核心接口。

commits.message:
[KERNELS] Support unscaled FP8 E4M3 matmul with FP16/BF16 (#11652)

Unscaled E4M3FN paired with FP16/BF16 currently fails
`triton_kernels.matmul` dtype or Hopper weight-layout checks. Both
kernels now widen only the FP8 tile to its partner's dtype before
`tl.dot`, preserving input storage and FP16 precision. The multiply uses
16-bit tensor cores.

Persistent kernels prefer FP8 on the MMA's lhs and use smaller K tiles
on Hopper. Account for staged inputs, widened RHS tiles and epilogue
scratch separately, leave Blackwell TMEM headroom, and select a fitting
epilogue before clamping stages. Keep gathered-input offsets separate
from the aligned base pointer when flattening persistent loops. AMD
sizes unscaled K tiles using the wider operand, so mixed FP8/16-bit
tiles fit gfx942 shared memory.

With the [unchanged upstream
compiler](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/2074a1b8a5cd283ce584f8ebca825c4f0b215fc1),
**520 mixed-dtype cases pass on H100 and 264 on GB300; all fail against
the base library**. The existing `test_op` grid now covers all four
mixed dtype pairs, both weight layouts, regular/persistent kernels,
bias, scaling and gather/scatter. Eight focused cases retain
memory-limit, default-planner and exact FP16 precision coverage. The 256
H100 / 128 GB300 skips are unchanged inapplicable inner-expert
combinations. Two existing FP16 gather/split-K and ragged-K cases also
pass on both libraries and GPUs.

AMD runtime CI passes all 132 newly enabled mixed cases on
[gfx942](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/actions/runs/34404235031/job/102643281846),
[gfx950](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/actions/runs/34404235031/job/102643281882),
and [gfx950 with ROCm
10.1](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/actions/runs/34404235031/job/102643281817),
including the 32 gfx942 cases that exceeded shared memory before the
tile-size fix. HIP retains its unsupported persistent/TMA exclusion.

### BF16

**Relative speed: BF16 × BF16 = 1.00×. Higher is faster.** Speed is
baseline latency divided by measured latency.

| GPU | M × N × K | FP8 × BF16 | BF16 × FP8 | FP8 × FP8 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 | 16 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.95× | 0.73× | 1.19× |
| H100 | 128 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.86× | 1.06× | 1.21× |
| H100 | 2048 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.85× | 0.85× | 1.90× |
| H100 | 4096 × 8192 × 8192 | 0.81× | 0.81× | 1.79×* |
| GB300 | 16 × 4096 × 4096 | 1.42× | 1.49× | 1.64× |
| GB300 | 128 × 4096 × 4096 | 1.42× | 1.32× | 1.61× |
| GB300 | 2048 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.96× | 0.96× | 1.97× |
| GB300 | 4096 × 8192 × 8192 | 0.86× | 0.94× | 1.84× |

**Peak tensor memory saved relative to BF16 × BF16. Higher means more
memory saved.**

| GPU | M × N × K | FP8 × BF16 | BF16 × FP8 | FP8 × FP8 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 | 16 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.1% | 46.7% | 46.9% |
| H100 | 128 × 4096 × 4096 | 1.0% | 32.0% | 33.0% |
| H100 | 2048 × 4096 × 4096 | 12.5% | 25.0% | 37.5% |
| H100 | 4096 × 8192 × 8192 | 12.5% | 25.0% | 37.5% |
| GB300 | 16 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.9% | 47.1% | 47.2% |
| GB300 | 128 × 4096 × 4096 | 4.8% | 34.6% | 35.5% |
| GB300 | 2048 × 4096 × 4096 | 12.5% | 25.0% | 37.5% |
| GB300 | 4096 × 8192 × 8192 | 12.5% | 25.0% | 37.5% |

Measured at [Size unscaled AMD matmul tiles for the wider
operand](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/a00f0cc854c41c23d895f2aedb7d14dc15849dbf).
FP8 means E4M3FN. Each GPU/shape uses identical E4M3-rounded values,
row-major A, column-major B, BF16 output, and default planner/precision
settings.

Latency is the median of five warm CUDA-graph measurements; input
conversion, compilation, and host dispatch are excluded. Peak active
PyTorch tensor allocation is measured separately after warmup in a fresh
process per case, before reference computation or graph capture. It
includes inputs, output, workspace, and cached library buffers; it
excludes CUDA context and unused allocator reservations. Five-sample
max–min spans reached 13.2% of the median on H100 and 3.3% on GB300.

For M ≥ 2048, mixed FP8/BF16 matmul delivers **0.81–0.85× BF16 speed on
H100** and **0.86–0.96× on GB300**, while saving about **12.5–25% peak
tensor memory**. Small-M results depend on GPU and operand order.

\* The largest H100 FP8 × FP8 case exceeds the default max-error
tolerance in four outputs (2.21% vs 2%; RMS 0.217% vs 0.4%). Its default
timing is shown. All other benchmark cases pass, including every mixed
case.

### FP16

Both FP16 × FP8 and FP8 × FP16 pass the existing grid and exact
precision tests: **260 cases on H100 and 132 on GB300**.

**Relative speed: FP16 × FP16 = 1.00×. Higher is faster.**

| GPU | M × N × K | FP8 × FP16 | FP16 × FP8 | FP8 × FP8 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 | 16 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.97× | 1.08× | 1.18× |
| H100 | 128 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.86× | 1.17× | 1.22× |
| H100 | 2048 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.98× | 1.01× | 1.95× |
| H100 | 4096 × 8192 × 8192 | 0.89× | 0.93× | 1.76× |
| GB300 | 16 × 4096 × 4096 | 1.41× | 1.48× | 1.63× |
| GB300 | 128 × 4096 × 4096 | 1.42× | 1.32× | 1.61× |
| GB300 | 2048 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.96× | 0.96× | 1.97× |
| GB300 | 4096 × 8192 × 8192 | 0.86× | 0.94× | 1.88× |

**Peak tensor memory saved relative to FP16 × FP16. Higher means more
memory saved.**

| GPU | M × N × K | FP8 × FP16 | FP16 × FP8 | FP8 × FP8 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 | 16 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.1% | 46.7% | 46.9% |
| H100 | 128 × 4096 × 4096 | 1.0% | 32.0% | 33.0% |
| H100 | 2048 × 4096 × 4096 | 12.5% | 25.0% | 37.5% |
| H100 | 4096 × 8192 × 8192 | 12.5% | 25.0% | 37.5% |
| GB300 | 16 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.9% | 47.1% | 47.2% |
| GB300 | 128 × 4096 × 4096 | 4.8% | 34.6% | 35.5% |
| GB300 | 2048 × 4096 × 4096 | 12.5% | 25.0% | 37.5% |
| GB300 | 4096 × 8192 × 8192 | 12.5% | 25.0% | 37.5% |

Measured at [Size unscaled AMD matmul tiles for the wider
operand](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/a00f0cc854c41c23d895f2aedb7d14dc15849dbf),
with the same input values, compiler and measurement protocol as the
BF16 section. All four arms produce FP16 output. All 32 benchmark cases
pass the default accuracy tolerances and finite-output checks.
Five-sample max–min spans reached 12.2% of the median on H100 and 5.1%
on GB300.

| Non-tests | +87 | -29 | +58 |
| All | +149 | -33 | +116 |

### Reviewer's guide

- `python/triton_kernels/triton_kernels/`: shared mixed-dot conversion,
Hopper layout support, tile and memory planning, and aligned
gathered-input addresses.
- `python/triton_kernels/tests/`: extend the existing matmul dtype grid;
retain focused resource-limit and FP16 precision regressions.

ascend_impact.functionality: 无影响。仅修改 python/test/gluon/test_core.py 中一个 Gluon 测试的布局参数化与 skip 门控，属于 Gluon/AMD 专属测试路径，Ascend 不使用 Gluon（编译到 TTGIR）也不运行该测试。

commits.message:
[AMD][Gluon] Run test_noinline_call_preserves_live_shared_allocation (#11684)

`test_noinline_call_preserves_live_shared_allocation` is gated on
`is_ampere_or_newer()`, but nothing in it is NVIDIA specific. The gate
is there because the layouts hardcode `threads_per_warp = 32`, which is
wrong on CDNA.

Pass `THREADS_PER_WARP` in as a constexpr, the way the rest of the file
already builds layouts. Thus the test can run on HIP too.

Also AMD has no equivalent coverage. `noinline` does not appear anywhere
under `third_party/amd/python/test`, so nothing was checking that a
noinline call preserves a live shared allocation there.

### Tests

Both kernels build for `gfx942` with the same shared size (1024) and
`noinline` count as on CUDA. Generated code on CUDA is unchanged apart
from the mangled callee name and line numbers. I have no AMD hardware,
so the numerics are for CI to confirm.
